open_points.subject: M11 OwnerSession timing facts and A13 session limits
open_points.text: M11 carries “the instant it began, its expiry at the latest” and “the instant of its last request”; State 1 says “Every time Registry records is an instant in UTC with time zone”, while A13 says the limits are measured by “the process's monotonic clock, which a change of the wall clock does not move”.
open_points.question: What timing facts does M11 actually store and use so that its UTC instants and stated expiry remain consistent with authoritative monotonic deadlines after the wall clock changes?
options: Store both UTC instants and separate monotonic deadlines, declaring which are authoritative
Make the M11 timing facts monotonic values and exempt them from State 1's UTC rule
Store only UTC instants but define how their displayed expiry is revised after wall-clock changes
open_points.default_guess: Store UTC instants for recorded facts plus private monotonic began, last-request and deadline values; use only the monotonic values for validity.

open_points.subject: Owner request admission versus the expiry pass
open_points.text: “Validity is checked when a request arrives”; state-changing requests take the session lock “after passing the session check”; the expiry pass takes the session lock and decides under it; and “a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs”.
open_points.question: What happens when a request passes the arrival-time session check but, before it acquires the session lock or records its arrival, the expiry pass acquires that lock and ends the session?
options: Admission and the last-request update are atomic under the session lock, so the pass cannot end an admitted session first
The expiry pass may end it, but the already admitted request still completes without recreating session state
The expiry pass wins and the previously admitted request is refused
open_points.default_guess: Make validation and the arrival-based last-request update atomic under the session lock; once admitted, let the request complete even if a later pass ends the session.

open_points.subject: A13 expiry-pass scheduling
open_points.text: “Registry ends it ... at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the start”; each pass takes the import lock and then session locks, which may already be held.
open_points.question: If a pass is still running or blocked when another 60-second boundary arrives, are missed passes queued, skipped, coalesced into one pass, or does completion shift the cadence?
options: Skip missed boundaries and keep the cadence anchored to process start
Coalesce all missed boundaries into one immediate pass
Queue one pass for every missed boundary
Run 60 seconds after the preceding pass completes
open_points.default_guess: Use one non-overlapping scheduler, coalesce missed boundaries, and keep future boundaries anchored to process start.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and “A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long”; no encryption construction, authentication mode, nonce rule, key derivation, or handling of keys longer than 32 bytes is declared.
open_points.question: What exact authenticated-encryption format and key-handling rules must every release use to create and verify a backup?
options: Use a declared AEAD algorithm with a fresh random nonce and derive a fixed-size encryption key from the configured bytes
Require an exact raw-key length and use it directly with a declared AEAD algorithm
Permit each release to choose its own encryption construction and record its format version
open_points.default_guess: Declare a versioned AES-256-GCM format, derive a 32-byte key with HKDF-SHA-256 from the configured key bytes, and generate a fresh 96-bit random nonce per backup.

open_points.subject: A18 unencrypted backup record
open_points.text: A backup records metadata “readable without its key”, and “a kept file's record is valid when its instant, release, last sequence number and key digest can all be read”; unreadable records are deleted, but the text does not say whether that record is cryptographically bound to the encrypted store.
open_points.question: Is the unencrypted record merely parseable and trusted as read, or must its values be authenticated against the ciphertext before they control listing, retention, deletion, restore-key selection, and the recorded sequence check?
options: Bind the whole record to the ciphertext as authenticated associated data
Put an authenticated copy inside the ciphertext and compare it after decryption, while treating the outer record as advisory
Treat readable outer metadata as valid without cryptographic authentication
open_points.default_guess: Bind the complete unencrypted record to the ciphertext as AEAD associated data and require authenticated verification whenever the applicable key is available; never treat unauthenticated metadata as proof of backup contents.

open_points.subject: A18 scheduling after a forward wall-clock change
open_points.text: A run starts at the first look at or after 03:00 when “an earlier look of the same process saw that date before 03:00”, but the text also says “A clock set forward past 03:00 of a date gives that date no run, the earlier look having seen another date”.
open_points.question: If the clock moves forward from before 03:00 to after 03:00 within the same UTC date, does that date run because the earlier look saw the same date, or is every forward jump past 03:00 treated as a missed run?
options: Run when the earlier observation was before 03:00 on the same UTC date
Skip whenever a wall-clock jump crosses 03:00, even within one date
Run only when the observed elapsed wall-clock step is within a declared tolerance
open_points.default_guess: Run it because the explicit same-date observation condition is satisfied; only a jump from another UTC date skips it.
